$$

Points $A$ and $C$ are shown in the picture above. Find $|\overset{\to }{AC}|.$
q-18057.worked_solution:
From the picture, we obtain $A(0,3)$ and $C(4,0).$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{OA}=a=0i+3j, \\  & \overset{\to }{OC}=c=4i+0j.\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing $\overset{\to }{AC}$ as the difference of position vectors, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AC} & =\overset{\to }{OC}-\overset{\to }{OA} \\  & =c-a \\  & =(4i)-(3j) \\  & =4i-3j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{\to }{AC}| & =\sqrt{(4)^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+9} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $A(0,3)$ and $B(4,-1).$ Find $|\overset{\to }{AB}|.$ Do not round the answer.

$|\overset{\to }{AB}|=$
{{field-1}}
q-320965.worked_solution:
We have 

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{OA}=a=0i+3j, \\  & \overset{\to }{OB}=b=4i-j.\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing $\overset{\to }{AB}$ as the difference of position vectors, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =\overset{\to }{OB}-\overset{\to }{OA} \\  & =b-a \\  & =(4i-j)-(0i+3j) \\  & =4i-4j.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{\to }{AB}| & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+16} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-70415.problem: Let $r=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $s=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $3r+2s$ and points the same direction.
q-70415.worked_solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction., we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{3r+2s}{|3r+2s|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}3r+2s & =3\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+2\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-6)+0 \\ 3+(-6)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|3r+2s| & =\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{45} \\  & =3\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $3r+2s$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{3r+2s}{|3r+2s|} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}(3r+2s) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
